text:
lucy: FYI saw a spike of short reconnects right after we flipped routing.policy=region-strict for ap-east. Console shows socket_down and route_failures, but the streaming events panel is almost flat. sampling+agg-lag?

omar: was that the routing change that forces tenant->regional-pool binding?

lucy: yes. timeline: deploy 11:00 -> spike at 11:03. lots of 101->close loops.

chen: samples? iirc we set streaming sampling to 1/200 for very chatty tenants. canary traffic gets lost under that.

deploy-bot: deploy 1809002400 applied to service/router-canary at 11:00:12 by ci-cd

lucy: pasted proxy trace: 

```
11:03:05 conn=aa11 route=ap-east tenant=edu-prod event=upgrade 101
11:03:05 conn=aa11 event=close reason=proxy.reset
11:03:05 conn=aa11 reconnect backoff=120ms sampled=false
```

lucy: sampled=false so no stream.event metrics emitted. console side panels show routing.errors but no streaming churn. ops escalate risk: customers see flakiness but billing/quotas appear unchanged.

omar: two problems: (1) visibility blindspot during rollouts, (2) quotas not reflecting reconnect attempts (could undercharge or mask issues).

chen: quick mitigation: force sampling override for requests with header `x-rollout-candidate: 1` for 15m. emit a low-cardinality probe on upgrade/close paths. probe must be telemetry-only and not increment quotas.

lucy: agree. also thinking about routing-side change: when region-strict rejects previous sticky route, we should emit `route_fallback=1` metric before closing so console can correlate.

omar: sketch: 

```
# proxy pseudocode
if req.headers['x-rollout-candidate']=='1':
  metrics.sampling.rate = 1.0
  metrics.emit('stream.probe', {telemetry_only: 'true', rollout_id: req.headers['x-rollout-id'] or 'canary-1809002400'})

on route_reject:
  metrics.emit('route.fallback', {reason: 'region-strict', telemetry_only: 'true'})
```

chen: important: rollout_id tag adds cardinality. only include rollout_id when header present and strip tenant id from tags. also mark telemetry_only to prevent billing.

deploy-bot: incident INC-2333 created: "ap-east routing canary: reconnects w/o streaming metrics" assigned to @lucy priority=P2

lucy: console asks for a small UX change: add a banner during rollouts saying "Streaming metrics may be sampled during high-volume routes. Use rollout filter to view all probe events." and add a sample_fraction indicator on streaming panels.

omar: also change the rollout playbook: if reconnect_rate > 150/min and probe_count < 50 in 5m then pause rollout and fallback to previous routing policy. otherwise keep canary and keep sampling override for 30m.

chen: on quotas: ensure probe emits do not affect quota math. but reconnects that actually fetch tokens should still be counted. if token-fetch is short-circuited by cache_hit we should still emit a counter `billing.intent=true` so finance can reconcile. boolean only.

lucy: good call. dashboard panel plan: two small panels side-by-side: (A) sum(stream.probe) by rollout_id (B) socket_closes with sample_fraction overlay. console-bot: can you create noise-free default?

console-bot: created panel PR D-4321: adds probe panel and sample_fraction pill. will gate showing rollout_id tag behind "enable rollout metrics" toggle.

omar: implementation plan: (1) sampling override for rollout header (proxy PR), (2) emit stream.probe + route.fallback markers, (3) add billing.intent boolean on cached-token fast-path, (4) console banner + panels, (5) add rollout controller auto-pause rule.

lucy: timeline: toggle sampling override now, probe emit in next 10m, console panel in 45m, auto-pause rule in next deploy window. i'll open PRs and link here.

chen: quick test case: simulate 100 reconnects with rollout header and verify probe_count ~= 100 while sample_fraction in UI shows 1.0. also verify quotas unchanged for telemetry_only events.

lucy: thanks everyone. posting PRs: proxy sampling override -> https://git.internal/r/router/+/2421, probe+fallback -> https://git.internal/r/router/+/2422. will update once merged.

omar: thx. leave this thread for async updates. :thumbsup:
